$comment: Per-dialect capability descriptor. An agent reads this AFTER the http-mcp `transports` tool tells it MQTT is adapter-provided. Declares how this dialect maps down onto the wire's two atoms.

maps_to.session: CHANNEL (bidi_command) — one held connection to the broker per node, dialled OUT (no inbound port; sandbox-safe); the node produces into it (PUBLISH) and consumes from it (deliveries)
maps_to.commands: frames on the CHANNEL — the far end publishes an envelope to <prefix>/commands/<ulid> (QoS 1) proposing ONE wire atom: a CALL (http_request shape) or a seat-addressed CHANNEL command (bidi_command shape)
maps_to.receipts: frames on the CHANNEL — the host fires the atom through the witness (8 collector /fetch or /run) and publishes a thick receipt, X-8-Witness inside, to <prefix>/receipts/<ulid> (QoS 1, RETAINED)
maps_to.presence: frames on the CHANNEL — <prefix>/presence/<node>, retained + last-will: the held connection made visible to the other side

capability_shaped: QoS 1 at-least-once (PUBACK) both ways; QoS 2 deliberately not offered — exactly-once belongs to the receipt (idempotent by ULID), not the transport
retain: receipts and presence are retained, so a far end that was away still finds its answer
persistent session (CleanSession=false) on the host: the broker queues commands while the host is down — store-and-forward without polling
keep-alive (PINGREQ/PINGRESP), last-will presence, username/password, TLS (mqtts://, CA file)
authority split: far end PROPOSES, host-side Policy DECIDES what fires (inbound) and what the receipt may carry back (egress: body/headers)
auth_slot resolution host-side (slots file) — no credential ever enters a topic
why_not_wire: A broker session IS a held duplex connection, so MQTT reduces to the CHANNEL atom and nothing else — but topics, QoS, retain, wills and persistent sessions are application delivery logic, not a transport shape. The adapter holds the broker connection, routes envelopes and receipts by topic, and presents CHANNEL frames upward; the wire never learns about topics. (Contrast gitbroker: a commit holds no connection, so git collapses CHANNEL into CALL. A broker pushes, so here the far end gets its receipt without polling.)

carries.call: http_request — fired by the host via the witness POST /fetch
carries.channel: bidi_command — fired by the host via the witness POST /run?session=<seat> (the far end names a seat, never a ws_url)

shape_proven_by: mqtt_test.go — both nodes dial out to a broker we own (broker.go, stdlib): a CALL envelope and a CHANNEL envelope each round-trip far end → broker → host → witness stub (X-8-Witness stamped) → retained receipt → far end; a command published while the host is DOWN is delivered when it returns (persistent session); a duplicate ULID is skipped; policy refuses and gates egress; a credential header is rejected; will/retain/wildcard/QoS1 proven at the client layer. Also `loopback mqtt`. Set MQTT_TEST_BROKER=mqtt://host:1883 to run the same round-trip against a real broker (mosquitto).
